author: olstakh
body:
For some reason from visual studio sometimes we observe AD0001 warning: 
```
Analyzer 'ReferenceProtector.Analyzers.ReferenceProtectorAnalyzer' threw an exception of type 'System.IO.FileNotFoundException' with message 'Could not load file or assembly 'System.Text.Json, Version=9.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified.'.
```

Even though this works via command line (i.e. `dotnet build`). Researching online - it's possible VS is a bit behind in dependency management of the analyzers (potentially, other IDEs might be too). Some suggest including the dependency in the package in `dotnet/analyzer/cs` folder, that's what's done in this PR

- [x] Update server/channel list to Discord-style sidebar layout
- [x] Add responsive design improvements
- [x] Update backend JavaScript to support new template structure
- [x] Make authentication page less prominent in design

**Phase 3: Message System Improvements** ✅
- [x] Support large text (# prefix) and Discord-style markdown formatting

- [x] Enhanced markdown support: bold, italic, strikethrough, code blocks, spoilers

**Phase 5: Media and Responsiveness** ✅
- [x] Fix image sizing on mobile devices with responsive CSS
- [x] Enhanced mobile layout with better breakpoints
- [x] Implement Discord embed rendering with proper styling
- [x] Improved emoji sizing for mobile devices
- [x] Better responsive message layout for small screens

**Phase 6: Additional Polish** ✅
- [x] Comprehensive responsive design across all templates
- [x] Enhanced image handling with proper aspect ratios
- [x] Discord-style embed rendering with thumbnails and metadata
- [x] Mobile-optimized emoji picker and interface elements
- [x] Performance considerations with conditional loading

### 🎉 **COMPLETED** - All Major Requirements Addressed

### Key Features Implemented:

**Modern Discord-Style Interface:**
- Three-panel layout (servers, channels, content) matching Discord
- Discord color scheme (#36393f, #2f3136, #5865f2, etc.)
- Whitney font stack with fallbacks
- Proper hover effects and animations

**Enhanced Message Experience:**
- Discord-style markdown (bold, italic, strikethrough, code blocks, spoilers)
- Large text support for messages starting with "#"
- User mention highlighting in yellow for current user
- Role-based username colors and proper display name hierarchy
- Timezone-aware message timestamps

**Mobile & Responsive Design:**
- Responsive breakpoints for tablet (768px) and mobile (480px)
- Proper image scaling and aspect ratio preservation
- Mobile-optimized emoji picker and interface elements
- Flexible layout that adapts to screen size

**Advanced Features:**
- Discord embed rendering with thumbnails and metadata
- Enhanced emoji sizing (larger for emoji-only messages)
- Automatic timezone detection and cookie storage
- Improved drawing interface with color palette

**Maintained Compatibility:**
- Full backward compatibility with existing functionality
- Support for legacy browsers and devices
- Graceful degradation when JavaScript is unavailable
- Preserved all existing features while enhancing UX

### Technical Achievements:
- **0 Breaking Changes** - All existing functionality preserved
- **Cross-Browser Compatible** - Works on modern and legacy browsers
- **Mobile-First Responsive** - Optimized for all screen sizes
- **Performance Optimized** - Conditional loading and efficient rendering

This overhaul successfully modernizes Discross to closely match Discord's look and feel while maintaining its core mission of supporting all platforms that support HTML.

*This pull request was created as a result of the following prompt from Copilot chat.*
> This pull request will address a comprehensive UI/UX overhaul for the Discross app, including but not limited to the following tasks:
> 
> 1. Simplify and modernize the send message bar and any related UI elements; ensure it does not extend beyond its box even on modern browsers and is visually simpler and more intuitive. Make send boxes consistent across both the message list and the drawing canvas.
> 2. Track when a channel was last viewed. Bold channels in the list if there are unread messages since last view. Add a horizontal red <hr> indicator for new messages loaded since last view.
> 3. When a user is pinged, highlight it in yellow. Remove underlines from messages. Make quoted messages use Discord's style.
> 4. Support large text (if a message starts with '# '), and proper Discord-style markdown formatting (code, asterisks, underscores, etc.).
> 5. Show display usernames for members, unless they have a display nickname. Show role colors next to names and bold names. Fix role pings display.
> 6. Use the user's local timezone if detectable (fallback to UTC otherwise). Detect via browser or IP.
> 7. Remove Discords/servers from the list if the user is no longer a member, or if the bot leaves; remove from blacklist if re-added. Replace missing server icons with an abbreviation (up to 5 chars) in theme-appropriate color. Remove animated GIF server icons.
> 8. Fix images showing up tiny on mobile; fix emoji rendering (not tiny, bigger if only emoji). Make inline emoji toggleable. Use Discord's font stack if available.
> 9. Render Discord embeds in messages. Make links styled as buttons where useful, and map channel links to appropriate web pages.
> 10. Revamp the homepage for better formatting (keep all info, avoid emoji). Make the authentication-required page less prominent and not red.
> 11. Drawing interface: Fix drawing send, add more pen colors, and improve drawing quality.
> 12. General: Polish all UI/UX to more closely match Discord's modern interface (color, layout, spacing, theme consistency, responsive, etc.).
> 
> Notes:
> - Prioritize UI clarity, theme consistency, and robust feature support.
> - Avoid breaking existing major workflows.
> - Reference Discord's UI/UX patterns where possible.
> - Avoid emoji as icons for homepage formatting.
> - Use best-effort for features that require unavailable Discord intents.
> 
> This overhaul should significantly modernize and improve the Discross UI and usability, aiming for a closer match to Discord's look and feel.

author: paulomacedodev
body:
This commit introduces the ability for players to join a match as stand-ins if the main player slots are full.

Key changes:
- `MatchDTO` and `Match` models now include `amountStandin` to define the number of stand-in slots.
- `MatchRepository`:
    - `joinToMatch`: Allows players to join as stand-ins if main slots are full and stand-in slots are available. Updates `standinPlayersInMatch` count in Firestore.
    - `checkStatusPlayerInMatch`: Now checks both main players and stand-in players.
    - `getPlayersInMatch`: Returns a `PlayersInMatch` object containing lists of both main and stand-in players.
    - `leaveToMatch`: Handles leaving from either main player or stand-in player lists, updating respective counts and reopening the match if it was full.
- `CreateMatch`: Sets a default `amountStandin` of 4 when creating a new match.
- `PlayersInMatch.kt`: New data class to hold separate lists for main and stand-in players.
- `MatchDetails.kt`:
    - Displays stand-in players in a separate RecyclerView (`recyclerStandIn`).
    - Updates UI labels to show stand-in player counts.
- `MatchDetailsViewModel`:
    - Added `_standinPlayersInMatch` LiveData to hold the list of stand-in players.
    - `getPlayersInMatch` now populates both `_playersInMatch` and `_standinPlayersInMatch`.

author: cdiddy77
body:
## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive support for **AWS S3** and **Google Cloud Storage** providers to the existing pluggable storage system, enabling multi-cloud storage capabilities with intelligent routing.

### 🚀 New Storage Providers

#### **AWS S3 Provider**
- Full async implementation using `aioboto3`
- CloudFront CDN integration for global content delivery
- Presigned URLs for direct client uploads/downloads
- Server-side encryption support (AES256, KMS)
- Multiple storage classes for cost optimization
- Comprehensive error handling with exponential backoff

#### **Google Cloud Storage Provider**  
- Full async implementation with thread pool execution
- Cloud CDN integration for fast global delivery
- Multiple authentication methods:
  - Service account JSON file
  - Service account JSON string (environment variable)
  - Default credentials (gcloud, workload identity, etc.)
- Proper metadata handling with GCS-specific validation

### 🏗️ Architecture Improvements

#### **Lazy Initialization Pattern**
Both providers now use lazy client initialization:
- ✅ **Testable**: Can instantiate without real cloud credentials
- ✅ **Fail Fast**: Errors occur only during actual usage, not configuration
- ✅ **Consistent**: Same pattern across all storage providers

#### **Intelligent Routing**
Configure different providers for different use cases:
```yaml
routing_rules:
  - condition: { size_gt: "50MB" }
    provider: "s3"  # Large files to S3
  - condition: { artifact_type: "image" }
    provider: "gcs"  # Images to GCS with CDN
```

### 📦 Dependencies & Installation

**Optional Dependencies:**
```bash
# For S3 support
pip install boards-backend[storage-s3]

# For GCS support  
pip install boards-backend[storage-gcs]

# For both
pip install boards-backend[storage-s3,storage-gcs]
```

### 🧪 Testing

- **80 comprehensive tests** covering all providers and scenarios
- **Mock-based testing** - no real cloud credentials required for development
- **Error scenario coverage** - authentication, network, and validation failures
- **Lazy initialization verification** - ensures providers instantiate safely

### 📚 Documentation

- **Complete provider documentation** with configuration examples
- **Best practices guide** for security, performance, and cost optimization
- **Migration strategies** for moving between providers
- **Example configurations** for development, staging, and production

### 🔧 Configuration Example

```yaml
storage:
  default_provider: "s3"
  providers:
    s3:
      type: "s3"
      config:
        bucket: "my-boards-bucket"
        region: "us-east-1"
        cloudfront_domain: "cdn.boards.io"
        upload_config:
          ServerSideEncryption: "AES256"
          StorageClass: "STANDARD"
    gcs:
      type: "gcs" 
      config:
        bucket: "my-boards-media"
        project_id: "boards-production"
        cdn_domain: "media.boards.io"
  routing_rules:
    - condition: { artifact_type: "model", size_gt: "100MB" }
      provider: "s3"
    - condition: { artifact_type: "image" }
      provider: "gcs"
    - provider: "s3"  # Default fallback
```

### ✅ Backward Compatibility

- **Fully backward compatible** with existing storage system
- **Existing providers unchanged** - local and Supabase providers work as before
- **Graceful degradation** when optional dependencies are not installed

## Test plan

- [x] All existing storage tests continue to pass
- [x] New S3 provider tests pass without real AWS credentials
- [x] New GCS provider tests pass without real GCP credentials  
- [x] Factory integration tests verify provider creation and error handling
- [x] Lazy initialization prevents credential errors during testing
- [x] Provider routing works correctly based on configuration
- [x] Documentation examples are valid and complete

### Motivation
<!-- Why make this change? Describe the problem, not the solution. This can also be a link to an issue. -->

I would like to get to a world where we never modify the arguments of an `ast::Send` node after it is created.  `Send::setBlock` is an impediment to doing this, so I would like to remove it.

This PR takes care of all the uses in `local_vars`.

We do have to construct an entirely new `ast::Send` node as a result, so there is some memory churn associated with this, but `super` nodes are uncommon, so this performance hit should be in the noise.  I think constructing the arguments for the new send in a more straightforward way might balance out the memory churn.

author: ivanaaxd
body:
### Implement `Block Visualizer` Plugin

This PR introduces the `Block Visualizer` plugin, a new visualization component that renders graphs using detailed, interactive blocks. This new visualizer replaces the simple circle representation with informative blocks containing all node attributes, offering a more comprehensive view of the graph data.

Key Changes:

**Core**
* **Plugin Registration:** `pyproject.toml` has been updated to correctly register `block-visualizer` as a `visualizer` plugin via entry points.
* **Model Integration:** The `core` platform now correctly handles the `Block Visualizer` key and passes the `Graph` object to its `render` method.

**Data Sources**
* No changes were required in data source plugins, as the `Block Visualizer` operates on the standardized `Graph` model provided by the platform.

**Visualizers**
* **New Plugin:** Added the `block_visualizer` plugin, which correctly inherits from `VisualizerPlugin`.
* **Advanced Rendering:** The plugin's `render` method now generates a custom SVG string. This SVG includes rectangles for each node and text elements for displaying all node attributes (`key: value` pairs).
* **Dynamic Sizing:** The height of each block is dynamically calculated based on the number of attributes to ensure all information is visible.

**Web (Django)**
* **Visualizer Switching:** Updated templates (`explorer.html`) to include buttons for switching between `Simple` and `Block` visualizers, controlled by a URL parameter.
* **Improved Context:** The `home` view (`views.py`) now dynamically uses the `visualizer_key` from the URL to render the correct visualization plugin.

**Frontend**
* **Interactive Functionality:**
    * **Pan & Zoom:** Integrated `D3.js` to enable seamless panning and zooming on the graph.
    * **Drag & Drop:** Nodes are now draggable, and connected edges automatically update their positions as nodes are moved.
    * **Event Handling:** Correctly handled `mousedown` events on the entire node group by setting `pointer-events: none` on text elements, preventing them from blocking mouse interactions.
* **Cross-Visualizer Synchronization:** The system now **persists node positions** when switching between `Block` and `Simple` visualizers, ensuring the layout is remembered. This enhances the user experience by maintaining a consistent view.

**How To Run**
1. `python -m venv .venv`
2. `.venv/Scripts/activate`
3. `cd ./graph-visualizer`
4. `pip install -e graph_visualizer`
5. `cd graph_visualizer`
6. `pip install -e api`
7. `cd plugins/data_source`
8. `pip install -e json_data_source`
9. `pip install -e xml_data_source`
10. `cd ..\..`
11. `pip install lxml`
12. `pip install django`
13. `pip install numpy`
14. `pip install networkx`
15. `python web/manage.py migrate`
16. `python web/manage.py runserver `

The main changes include adding reactions to issue comments to indicate the progress and status of the action, enhancing robustness of installation steps, and updating function signatures to support these new features. **GitHub Action workflow improvements:** * Installation steps for `pochi CLI`, `ripgrep`, and `bun` now include error handling to exit early and print clear error messages if any step fails. Dependency installation also provides feedback on failure. author: melvin-molder
body:
Summary:
Fix mixins so vault join and leave messages are correctly forwarded to Discord after Vault Hunters updates.

What I changed:
- MC2Discord: added `MixinPlayerList` to intercept `broadcastMessage` and forward vault-related messages via mc2discord.
- DCIntegration: Replaced `MixinClassicListenersLogic` with `MixinPlayerList` reliably capture join and leave messages with the updated Vault Hunters code.
- SDLink: Replaced `MixinClassicListenersLogic` with `MixinPlayerList` similarly for SDLink compatibility.
- Updated mixin configs so each integration only loads when its Discord mod is present.

Testing:
- Built locally and manually tested only with mc2discord; join/leave messages were sent to Discord.
- SDLink and DCIntegration behavior were updated but not manually tested here (require those mods installed to verify).

author: tremwil
body:
Notes:
- Due to [an incompatibility](https://github.com/ultrabug/mkdocs-static-i18n/issues/283) between the Material `blog` plugin and the `mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin, I opted to disable the `blog` plugin and manually write the nav for blogs instead. Some other workarounds exist but they are hacky and come with extra limitations (e.g. blogs being default language only).
- I copied over the `collapse-code` Markdown extension used by the pymdownx docs. It's looks much nicer than putting code blocks inside a `<details>` tag or using collapsible admonitions.
- To load a local extension without requiring PYTHONPATH to be set prior to running `mkdocs serve`, a hook had to be added to dynamically add it to the config after it's been validated. This is because mkdocs tries to load the extensions during `mkdocs.yml` config validation, which would fail before any custom hooks can run.

author: whitehackr
body:
## Summary

This PR implements comprehensive dbt architecture improvements that enable proper experimentation analysis:

### Key Changes

**Dataset Organization**
- Fixed dataset routing with custom schema macro using `flit_` prefix
- Models now deploy to proper datasets: `flit_staging`, `flit_intermediate`, `flit_marts`
- Eliminates the issue where all models were deployed to `flit_raw`

**Experiment Integration**  
- Added `experiment_assignments` as a dbt source with enhanced schema
- Integrated user assignments into `int_experiment_orders_union` via JOIN -- that is added control/treatment labels and experiment status columns

**Data Quality Improvements**
- Removed unused `returned_at` column (was problematic INT64 with all NULL values)
- Fixed column schema mismatches between baseline and synthetic data
- Updated deprecated dbt test syntax to modern format

### Technical Details

**New Architecture**
```
flit_staging/
├── stg_thelook_baseline_orders (baseline data)
└── stg_synthetic_overlay_orders (synthetic treatment effects)

flit_intermediate/  
└── int_experiment_orders_union (combined + assignments)
    ├── control_treatment (control/treatment labels) 
    ├── experiment_status (participant/non_participant)

flit_marts/
└── mart_free_shipping_threshold_analysis (analysis-ready)
```

### Testing

- ✅ All 4 dbt models run successfully
- ✅ Dataset organization working (proper flit_ prefixed datasets)
- ✅ Experiment assignments JOIN working correctly
- ✅ End-to-end data pipeline validated


### Impact
This enables Phase 3 statistical analysis by providing properly structured data with:
- User-level experiment assignments (control vs treatment)
- Combined baseline and synthetic overlay data
- Analysis-ready marts for statistical testing

Ready for experimentation analysis in flit-experiments repository.

author: copilot
body:
Resolves the GitHub Actions deployment failure that was occurring during the `npm install` step due to the absence of a `package.json` file.

## Problem
The `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` workflow was failing with the following error:
```
npm ERR! code ENOENT
npm ERR! errno -2
npm ERR! enoent ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'package.json'
```

This prevented the application from being deployed to GitHub Pages as the workflow couldn't install dependencies or run the build command.

## Solution
Added the missing `package.json` file with:

1. **Build Script Configuration**: A `build:frontend` script that copies all necessary frontend files (`index.html`, `app.js`, `styles.css`, `sw.js`, `assets/`, `public/`) to the `./build` directory as expected by the deployment workflow.

2. **Optional Dependencies**: Moved backend dependencies (`express`, `cors`, `sqlite3`, `puppeteer`) to `optionalDependencies` to avoid installing heavy packages during CI/CD since GitHub Pages only needs the static frontend files.

3. **Additional Scripts**: Added convenience scripts for local development (`dev`, `start`) and separate installation commands for backend dependencies when needed.

Also added a comprehensive `.gitignore` file to prevent committing:
- `node_modules/` and package lock files
- `build/` directory (generated during CI)
- Database files and other runtime artifacts

## Verification
The complete workflow now works correctly:
```bash
npm install    # ✅ Succeeds (installs no dependencies by default)
npm run build  # ✅ Creates ./build directory with all frontend files
```

This minimal approach fixes the immediate CI/CD issue while maintaining the existing application structure and avoiding unnecessary dependencies in the deployment pipeline.

body:
### ✅ US6: Brands can list licenses by customer email across all brands - FULLY IMPLEMENTED

**Status**: ✅ **FULLY IMPLEMENTED**

**Implementation Details**:
- **Cross-Brand License Listing**: `GET /api/v1/customers/licenses` - List all licenses for a customer across all brands
- **Brand-Specific License Listing**: `GET /api/v1/customers/licenses/brand` - List licenses for a customer within the authenticated brand
- **Comprehensive Customer Summary**: Complete overview of customer's license ecosystem
- **Multi-Brand Support**: Access to customer data across the entire ecosystem

**Features**:
- ✅ Brands can see customer licenses across all brands (requires authentication)
- ✅ Brand-specific customer license queries
- ✅ Comprehensive customer license summary with statistics
- ✅ Product and seat usage aggregation across brands
- ✅ License status breakdown (active, suspended, cancelled, expired)
- ✅ Brand relationship mapping for customers

**API Endpoints**:
```
GET /api/v1/customers/licenses?customer_email={email}
GET /api/v1/customers/licenses/brand?customer_email={email}
```

**Example Workflow**:
```bash
# 1. List all licenses for a customer across all brands
curl -X GET "http://localhost:8002/api/v1/customers/licenses?customer_email=user@example.com" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {brand-token}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"

# 2. List licenses for a customer within the authenticated brand
curl -X GET "http://localhost:8002/api/v1/customers/licenses/brand?customer_email=user@example.com" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {brand-token}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```

**Response Structure**:
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Successfully retrieved license information for customer user@example.com",
  "data": {
    "customer_email": "user@example.com",
    "total_license_keys": 2,
    "total_licenses": 3,
    "brands_count": 2,
    "brands": [
      {
        "uuid": "brand-uuid-1",
        "name": "RankMath",

This PR addresses all requirements from the problem statement by fixing the admin 500 error (already resolved) and implementing fully functional hostess dashboard shortcuts, transforming placeholder buttons into operational features with real-time data and user interactions.

## Changes Made

### 1. Admin 500 Error Resolution ✅
The admin 500 Internal Server Error was already resolved through the existing `findOne()` method implementation in the base `Model` class. All admin access functionality now works correctly without fatal errors.

### 2. Hostess Dashboard Improvements 🚀

**Before:** All shortcut buttons showed placeholder "en desarrollo" (in development) messages  
**After:** Fully functional buttons with AJAX-powered modals and real-time data

#### New API Endpoints in `HostessController.php`
- `quickCheckinData()` - Returns pending check-ins for today via AJAX
- `tableStatusData()` - Provides real-time table availability status  
- `createReservation()` - Handles new reservation creation with validation
- `reservationDetails($id)` - Fetches complete reservation information

#### Enhanced Reservation Model

#### Functional JavaScript Features
- **Quick Check-in Modal**: Shows pending reservations with direct check-in links
- **Table Status Modal**: Displays real-time table availability with customer information
- **New Reservation Form**: Complete form with validation, date/time pickers, and AJAX submission
- **Reservation Details Modal**: Comprehensive view with all reservation data and action buttons

### 3. Technical Improvements

**Error Handling**: Robust exception handling across all new endpoints  
**User Experience**: Bootstrap modal integration with smooth interactions  
**Data Validation**: Client-side and server-side form validation  
**Real-time Updates**: AJAX calls eliminate need for page reloads

### 4. Database Validation ✅
Confirmed the system uses MySQL exclusively with no SQLite references:
- Configuration uses MySQL PDO driver
- Database: `ejercito_multirestaurante` (MySQL)
- No SQLite dependencies found

### 5. Testing & Documentation
- Created comprehensive validation tests (`tests/hostess_dashboard_validation.php`)
- Added detailed documentation (`CHANGES_DOCUMENTATION.md`)
- All changes include descriptive comments explaining functionality
- Surgical modifications preserve existing functionality

- All shortcuts now perform actual operations instead of showing placeholder messages

## Files Modified

- `app/controllers/HostessController.php` - 4 new API methods (112 lines added)
- `app/models/Reservation.php` - 1 new method (12 lines added)  
- `app/views/hostess/dashboard.php` - Complete JavaScript functionality (220+ lines updated)
- `tests/hostess_dashboard_validation.php` - New validation tests
- `CHANGES_DOCUMENTATION.md` - Complete implementation documentation

## Impact

**✅ Zero Breaking Changes**: All modifications are additive, preserving existing functionality  
**✅ Enhanced User Experience**: Hostess staff can now perform all key actions from the dashboard  
**✅ Improved Efficiency**: Reduced clicks and page loads for common operations

> 1. Corregir el error 500 - Internal Server Error al acceder como nivel admin. Revisar logs, capturar y manejar excepciones, validar rutas y permisos, asegurando que el dashboard admin funcione correctamente.

author: copilot
body:
This PR completely refactors the Library of Bears codebase to implement clean architecture principles while maintaining all existing model entities. The refactoring adds comprehensive CRUD operations, secure JWT authentication, and file upload capabilities using MinIO.

## 🏗️ Architecture Transformation

The codebase has been restructured from a simple 3-layer architecture to a proper clean architecture implementation:

**Before:**
- Direct database access from controllers
- Limited CRUD operations
- Basic authentication without password hashing
- No file upload support

**After:**
- **Domain Layer**: Repository interfaces defining contracts
- **Infrastructure Layer**: MySQL implementations + MinIO file service
- **Use Case Layer**: Business logic with validation and error handling
- **Delivery Layer**: HTTP handlers with complete CRUD operations
- **Dependency Injection**: Clean IoC container pattern

## 🚀 Key Features Added

### Complete CRUD Operations
All models now have full CRUD support with proper relationships:
- **Users**: Registration, login, profile management with role-based access
- **Authors**: Complete lifecycle management
- **Series**: Full CRUD with author relationships
- **Arts**: Enhanced CRUD with file upload and author/series relationships

### Enhanced Security
- **JWT Authentication**: Token-based authentication with 72-hour expiry
- **Password Security**: bcrypt hashing for user passwords
- **Protected Routes**: Public read access, authenticated write operations
- **CORS Support**: Cross-origin resource sharing for web clients

### File Upload System
- **MinIO Integration**: Scalable object storage for arts files
- **Multipart Form Support**: Handle file uploads with metadata
- **Automatic Management**: Bucket creation and unique file naming
- **File URL Generation**: Direct access to uploaded files

## 📚 API Enhancements

### New Authentication Endpoints
```http
POST /auth/register  # User registration with password hashing
POST /auth/login     # Login with JWT token generation
```

### Complete CRUD Endpoints
All entities now support full CRUD operations with proper HTTP methods:
- `GET /users`, `PUT /users/:id`, `DELETE /users/:id` (protected)
- `POST /authors`, `PUT /authors/:id`, `DELETE /authors/:id` (protected)
- `POST /series`, `PUT /series/:id`, `DELETE /series/:id` (protected)
- `POST /arts`, `PUT /arts/:id`, `DELETE /arts/:id` (protected)

### File Upload Endpoints
```http
POST /arts/upload        # Create arts with file upload
PUT /arts/:id/upload     # Update arts with file upload
```

### Relationship Queries
```http
GET /series/author/:authorId   # Get series by author
GET /arts/author/:authorId     # Get arts by author
GET /arts/series/:seriesId     # Get arts by series
```

## 🛠️ Developer Experience

### Development Tools
- **Docker Compose**: MySQL + MinIO for local development
- **Setup Script**: `./dev-setup.sh` for automated environment setup
- **Comprehensive Documentation**: Complete API reference with cURL examples
- **Unit Tests**: Test suite for core functionality

### Environment Configuration
All services are configurable via environment variables:
```env
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=3307
DB_NAME=library_of_bears
SECRET=your-secret-key
MINIO_ENDPOINT=localhost:9000
MINIO_ACCESS_KEY=minioadmin
MINIO_SECRET_KEY=minioadmin
```

## 🔧 Technical Improvements

### Code Quality
- **Separation of Concerns**: Clear layer boundaries with proper abstractions
- **Dependency Injection**: Testable architecture with clean dependencies
- **Error Handling**: Consistent error responses across all endpoints
- **Type Safety**: Proper struct validation and type checking

### Performance & Scalability
- **Database Optimization**: Proper preloading of relationships
- **File Storage**: MinIO for scalable file handling
- **Connection Pooling**: GORM with MySQL connection management
- **Stateless Design**: JWT tokens enable horizontal scaling

### Security
- **Input Validation**: Proper request body validation
- **Authentication Middleware**: JWT verification for protected routes
- **Password Security**: Industry-standard bcrypt hashing
- **CORS Configuration**: Secure cross-origin request handling

## 📋 Migration Notes

### Backward Compatibility
- All existing model structures are preserved
- Database migrations will run automatically via GORM AutoMigrate
- Existing data remains intact

### New Dependencies
- `github.com/minio/minio-go/v7` for file storage
- `golang.org/x/crypto` for password hashing
- Enhanced middleware for CORS and authentication

## 🚀 Quick Start

1. **Start dependencies:**
   ```bash
   docker-compose up -d mysql minio
   ```

2. **Build and run:**
   ```bash
   ./dev-setup.sh
   ./BearLibrary
   ```

3. **Test the API:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:8000/healthcheck
   ```

The application provides the same functionality as before while adding comprehensive CRUD operations, secure authentication, and file upload capabilities in a maintainable, scalable architecture.

author: dzuelke
body:
The polyfill processing step yields quite a bit of interesting stats for `bin/report`:
- number of polyfills detected in userland dependencies
- number of resulting native package replacement attempts we made
- number of successful replacements
- number of resulting package installations
  - successful replacement does not necessarily mean we actually installed a package
  - could have merely been an activation
  - or a transient dependency was installed despite the polyfill
  - or we have more installs, because the replacement pulled in further dependencies
- sorted, comma-separated list of package names we could not install a native version of
  - which is fine, that's what polyfills are for, but we may be able to spot "prominent" missing native extensions as they emerge

Polyfill replacements had pretty thorough tests already, so building upon those.

GUS-W-19473512

author: copilot
body:
This PR introduces a proper Service and Data architecture for the Formula feature, replacing in-VM sample data usage with a Qt SQLite-backed repository while maintaining full backward compatibility.

## Problem

The current Formula feature loads sample data directly in the ViewModel:

```cpp
FormulaViewModel formulaVm;
formulaVm.loadSampleData(); // Hard-coded sample data in ViewModel
```

This approach has several limitations:
- **Tight coupling**: UI logic mixed with data generation
- **No persistence**: Data is recreated on every app start
- **Hard to extend**: Adding new data sources requires ViewModel changes
- **Testing difficulties**: Hard to test with different data sets

## Solution

Implemented a clean layered architecture following the repository pattern:

```cpp
// New architecture: Repository → Service → ViewModel
auto repository = std::make_shared<data::repositories::FormulaRepository>();
auto service = std::make_shared<domain::services::FormulaService>(repository);
auto viewModel = std::make_unique<FormulaViewModel>(service);
viewModel->loadData(); // Uses service, falls back to sample data if needed
```

### Key Components

**Domain Layer** (`fj_domain`):
- `domain/entities/Formula.h` - Pure C++ DTOs with no Qt dependencies
- `domain/repositories/IFormulaRepository.h` - Repository interface contract
- `domain/services/FormulaService.h` - Business logic coordination

**Data Layer** (`fj_data`):
- `data/repositories/FormulaRepository.cpp` - SQLite implementation with automatic table creation and sample data seeding

**Presentation Layer** (`fj_presentation_*`):
- Enhanced `FormulaViewModel` with optional service injection
- Updated `DataPage` to wire the complete service chain

### Backward Compatibility

The implementation maintains 100% backward compatibility:

```cpp
// Old code still works unchanged
FormulaViewModel formulaVm;
formulaVm.loadSampleData(); // ✅ Still works

// New service-based approach
FormulaViewModel formulaVm(service);
formulaVm.loadData(); // ✅ Uses service with automatic fallback
```

### Graceful Fallback

The system gracefully handles failure scenarios:
- **No service injected** → Uses sample data
- **Database file missing** → Creates new database with sample data
- **Database corruption** → Falls back to sample data
- **Service unavailable** → Falls back to sample data

### Database Schema

The SQLite implementation creates two tables:

```sql
CREATE TABLE formula_nodes (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    label TEXT NOT NULL,
    level INTEGER NOT NULL,      -- 0=category, 1=subcategory, 2=formula
    parent_id TEXT,
    sort_order INTEGER DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE TABLE formula_details (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    source TEXT,               -- e.g., "《伤寒论》"
    composition TEXT,          -- Drug composition
    usage TEXT,               -- Usage instructions
    function TEXT,            -- Effects and functions
    indication TEXT,          -- Main indications
    note TEXT                 -- Additional notes
);
```

## Testing

All existing tests pass, ensuring no regressions. New integration tests verify:
- Service chain works correctly with real database
- Fallback mechanisms activate when needed
- Data integrity is maintained across the architecture layers

## Benefits

1. **Clean Architecture**: Clear separation of concerns between Domain, Data, and Presentation
2. **Extensibility**: Easy to add new data sources (JSON, XML, network APIs) without UI changes
3. **Testability**: Each layer can be unit tested independently
4. **Reliability**: Multiple fallback mechanisms ensure the app always works
5. **Performance**: Database persistence eliminates data recreation overhead

The Formula feature now follows enterprise-grade architectural patterns while maintaining the existing user experience.

> Summary
> Introduce a proper Service and Data architecture for the Formula feature and remove in-VM sample data usage by default. Wire ViewModel → Service → Data, with a Qt SQLite-backed repository. Keep backward compatibility: if a database is not present or initialization fails, FormulaViewModel will fall back to its current sample-data path so the app still runs.
> 
> Goals
> - Define clear domain contracts (entities + repository + service) for Formulas.
> - Implement a data layer using Qt SQL (SQLite) to load the formula category tree and details from database tables.
> - Implement a domain service that uses the repository to supply the ViewModel.
> - Update FormulaViewModel to consume the service instead of populating in-VM sample data by default.
> - Provide an injection path from the presentation layer (DataPage) to set the service instance for the Formula feature, without breaking existing UI usage.
> - Update CMakeLists to link Qt6::Sql and compile the new files.
> 
> Constraints and context
> - The repo already has a layered build: fj_domain, fj_data, fj_presentation_vm, fj_presentation_pages, etc. DataPage builds UI using declarative widgets and currently constructs UiFormulaView.
> - FormulaViewModel currently builds a sample tree via loadSampleData(); the view calls this method.
> - We must not break current screens while switching to the new architecture; introduce graceful fallback.
> - We can’t assume a specific DB file path yet; use AppConfig or a conventional location in data/sources/local. If DB is missing, fallback to sample data.
> 
> Detailed plan
> 1) Domain layer (fj_domain)
>    - Add domain entities for Formulas:

author: kitzy
body:
The existing query used a CROSS JOIN with USING(id), which is not valid SQL in Fleet/SQLite and resulted in a syntax error when saving the query.

This change replaces the CROSS JOIN with a standard JOIN ... ON ... clause. The explicit ON form was chosen for clarity:

- Makes the join condition (c.id = p.id) obvious to readers
- Avoids the subtle column-merging behavior of USING

This preserves the intended behavior (joining containers with their processes by ID) while ensuring the query can be saved and run correctly in Fleet.

body:
This change improves the readability of generated markdown files by adding a blank line before each top-level task (except the first one). 

**Before:**
```markdown
# Title

- [ ] 1. Task 1
  - [ ] 1.1 Subtask 1.1
- [ ] 2. Task 2
```

**After:**
```markdown
# Title

- [ ] 1. Task 1
  - [ ] 1.1 Subtask 1.1

- [ ] 2. Task 2
```

## Implementation

The change is minimal and surgical:
- Modified `RenderMarkdown()` function in `internal/task/render.go` to add a newline before each top-level task after the first
- Updated corresponding tests to expect the new format
- Verified that JSON and table output formats remain unaffected

body:
## Summary
This PR extends Editor user permissions to customize the Order Entry Button size and position, adds persistent storage of custom settings, and implements user control over automatic system updates.

## Problem
- Editor users (id == 2) could not edit the Order Entry Button size/position
- Custom size changes were not being saved to the system data file
- Automatic `vt_data` downloads would overwrite custom settings
- No user control over when system updates occur

## Solution
1. **Extended Editor Permissions**: Modified `PosZone::CanEdit()` and `PosZone::CanCopy()` to allow Editor access to `ZONE_ORDER_ENTRY` zones
2. **Persistent Storage**: Added `SaveSystemData()` calls in `OrderEntryZone::SetSize()` and `OrderEntryZone::SetPosition()` methods
3. **Auto-Update Control**: Implemented "Auto-Update vt_data on Startup" soft switch with visual ON/OFF feedback
4. **Complete Workflow**: Editors can now customize, save, and control system updates

## Changes Made

### Files Modified:
- `zone/pos_zone.cc` - Extended Editor permissions for Order Entry Button
- `zone/order_zone.cc` - Added persistent storage of size/position changes
- `main/settings.hh` - Added auto-update setting and switch constant
- `main/settings.cc` - Implemented auto-update setting persistence
- `main/labels.cc` - Added switch name and value arrays
- `zone/settings_zone.cc` - Implemented soft switch logic and UI
- `main/manager.cc` - Added auto-update control in vt_data download logic
- `changelog.md` - Documented all changes

### Key Features:
- ✅ **Editor Access**: Editors can now edit Order Entry Button size/position
- ✅ **Persistent Storage**: Custom sizes automatically saved to `vt_data`
- ✅ **Visual Feedback**: Green "ON" / Red "OFF" status for auto-update setting
- ✅ **User Control**: Toggle automatic `vt_data` updates on/off
- ✅ **Backward Compatible**: Default auto-update enabled, existing functionality preserved

## Technical Details

### Permission Changes:
```cpp
// zone/pos_zone.cc
if (page->id < 0 && !e->CanEditSystem() && Type() != ZONE_ORDER_ENTRY)
    return 0;
return e->CanEdit();
```

### Persistent Storage:
```cpp
// zone/order_zone.cc
int size = page->size - 1;
Settings *s = t->GetSettings();
s->oewindow[size].SetRegion(x, y, w, h);
SaveSystemData(); // Added this line
```

### Auto-Update Control:
- New setting: `auto_update_vt_data` (default: enabled)
- Soft switch: "Auto-Update vt_data on Startup"
- Visual feedback: Green "ON" / Red "OFF" status
- Integrated with existing Soft Switches system

## Testing
- ✅ Build successful with no compilation errors
- ✅ Editor users can now edit Order Entry Button
- ✅ Custom sizes persist across program restarts
- ✅ Auto-update toggle works correctly
- ✅ Visual feedback displays proper ON/OFF status
- ✅ Backward compatibility maintained

## Impact
- **User Experience**: Editors can now customize their workspace
- **Data Persistence**: Custom settings are preserved across restarts
- **System Control**: Users have control over automatic updates
- **Security**: Maintains existing permission structure
- **Compatibility**: No breaking changes to existing functionality

## Related Issues
Fixes the limitation where Editor users could not customize the Order Entry Button and their changes would be lost on system updates.

This pull request introduces a comprehensive user profile system, including new backend routes, database fields, and frontend templates for viewing and editing user profiles. It also improves user feedback across the application by replacing alert dialogs with a consistent `showAlert` modal system.

**User Profile System Enhancements:**

- **Backend:**
  - Added new profile-related routes: `/perfil` (view own profile), `/perfil/editar` (edit profile), and `/perfil/<int:user_id>` (view other user's profile), with logic for privacy and statistics visibility. Also includes a helper function `ensure_profile_fields` to guarantee all profile fields are set and sensible defaults are provided.
  - Extended `UserModel` with new profile fields (`full_name`, `email`, `bio`, `avatar_url`, `location`, `birth_date`) and privacy/configuration fields (`is_public`, `show_stats`, `email_notifications`).

- **Frontend:**
  - Added a new `edit_profile.html` template with a modern, user-friendly form for editing profile information, avatar preview, privacy toggles, and real-time validation. Includes JavaScript for AJAX form submission and improved user experience.
  - Updated the navigation bar in `base.html` to link to the user's profile page, highlighting the active section for better navigation clarity.

**User Feedback Improvements:**

- Replaced all `alert()` calls with the asynchronous `showAlert()` modal for consistent, user-friendly notifications across various templates (`index.html`, `all_movies.html`, `friend_lists.html`). This applies to both success and error messages, improving the overall UX. author: guilherme-soares-sequeira
body:
This branch contains support for both polybench 4.2 and dataset sizes.
The former has been added in the likeness of all other benchmarks, though I did have to also add support for additional source files to avoid duplication.

The way the BenchmarkSuites are defined has been refactored. Now, every BenchmarkSuite has a class of its own, extending a base generic BenchmarkSuite class. It must be parameterized with an enum describing which possible sizes it allows. If one of the suite's apps doesn't allow one of the input sizes, it must declare so in the "invalidInputSizes" array at its declaration. Naturally, this means that AppSummary also has to be parameterized.
The loadSuite and loadApp have also been extended to accommodate these features, though they have been done so in a backwards compatible way. If the user does not specify which input sizes to use, loadSuite iterates over all possible sizes. If loadApp doesn't receive an input size then it assumes there is none, and therefore adds no flags.

However, it seems I cannot compile many of the test suites, with errors such as:
```
/tmp/clang_ast_exe/clang_includes/1-libcxx_12.0.0/cstddef:44:15: fatal error: 'stddef.h' file not found

              ^~~~~~~~~~
1 error generated.
Error while processing /tmp/__clava_woven_8c03eb3f-0f97-4af2-b234-65d0af436cce/utils.h.
```

In this case, I was attempting to test the Rosetta-Single suite. I do not currently have the time to fix these issues, so further testing is still needed.

Additionally, the sizes for cortexsuite-vision still need to be added.

author: copilot
body:
The outdoor activity list was appearing blank because the feature required GPS coordinates for distance calculations but didn't automatically request location permission. This PR implements a smart location request flow with graceful fallback behavior.

## Problem

When users clicked "🏞️ Find Outdoor Activities", they saw only a message saying "📍 Location access needed for activity recommendations" instead of the expected list of activities. The data collection was working correctly (9 activities were successfully loaded into IndexedDB), but the UI workflow had a critical gap.

## Solution

### Automatic Location Request
- Modified `findOutdoorActivities()` to automatically request location permission when needed
- Added dedicated `requestLocationForActivities()` method with 10-second timeout
- Provides clear status updates during the location request process

### Graceful Fallback
- Enhanced `updateActivityRecommendations()` to work without location data
- Created `getAllActivitiesWithoutDistance()` method for location-free display  
- Modified `displayActivityRecommendations()` to handle missing distance/travel time data

### Improved User Experience
- **Before**: Blank list requiring manual permission setup
- **After**: Immediate activity display with smart location enhancement
- Activities show "Location needed for distance" instead of failing completely
- All filtering functionality works regardless of location availability

## Technical Implementation

The changes maintain backward compatibility while adding robust error handling:

```javascript
// New workflow in findOutdoorActivities()
if (!this.currentPosition) {
    try {
        await this.requestLocationForActivities();
    } catch (error) {
        // Falls back to showing activities without distance
        console.log('Location request failed, showing activities without distance:', error);
    }
}
```

Activities now display with appropriate messaging:
- With location: "📍 2.5 km away" and "🕐 15 min drive"  
- Without location: "📍 Location needed for distance" and "🕐 Unknown travel time"

## Data Collection Validation

✅ **Sample data loading**: 9 outdoor activities successfully initialized  
✅ **Activity filtering**: Works correctly for hiking, fishing, cycling, etc.  
✅ **Database structure**: Proper IndexedDB schema with activity type indexes  
✅ **Search tracking**: Activity searches saved for export functionality  
✅ **Error handling**: Graceful degradation when location/weather unavailable  

The outdoor activity feature is now fully functional with proper user guidance and robust fallback behavior.

## Screenshots

![Outdoor Activities Working](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3de8d075-d292-483a-ad07-941af5194a19)

*The activity list now displays all available outdoor activities with clear information about distance requirements*

Fixes #19.

This change fixes the issue by:

This ensures the controllers are correctly synchronized, and the UI behaves as expected.

author: shubbu03
body:
### Problem
When working with multiple signers in Solana applications, developers often need to load the same keypair from different sources (files, environment variables, etc.). Currently, each call to loadKeypairSigner* functions creates a new TransactionSigner instance, even when loading the same underlying keypair.
This leads to the ```SOLANA_ERROR__SIGNER__ADDRESS_CANNOT_HAVE_MULTIPLE_SIGNERS``` error when attempting to sign transactions that contain multiple instances of signers with the same address. This is a common issue in complex applications where:
- The same keypair serves multiple roles (fee payer + authority)
- Keypairs are loaded from multiple sources for redundancy
- Reusable functions independently load the same keypair
- Transaction builders accept multiple signers that might be the same
- The error prevents legitimate use cases and forces developers to write boilerplate deduplication logic.

### Summary of Changes
Core Implementation
- Enhanced ```loadKeypairSignerFromFile()``` , ```loadKeypairSignerFromEnvironment()``` , ```loadKeypairSignerFromEnvironmentBase58()``` with optional existingSigner parameter

Deduplication Logic

```
// If an existing signer is provided and has the same address, return it for deduplication
if (existingSigner && existingSigner.address === newSigner.address) {
  return existingSigner as KeyPairSigner;
}
return newSigner;
```
Key Features
- Address-based comparison - Compares signer addresses to detect duplicates
- Backward compatible - All existing code continues to work without changes
- Type safe - Maintains full TypeScript support and proper return types
- Cross-method deduplication - Works across different load methods (file, env, base58)

Testing

13 comprehensive tests covering all scenarios:
- Basic deduplication functionality
- Cross-method deduplication
- Edge cases (undefined parameters, different addresses)
- Real-world scenarios preventing the actual error
- Type safety validation

Documentation
- Complete documentation section in ```/docs/content/docs/getting-started/signers.mdx```
- Usage examples showing when and how to use deduplication
- Best practices for production applications
- Real-world scenarios with code examples

Fixes # 
this pr fixes issue #125

author: desmondc65
body:
# Summary
This PR introduces a standalone Python utility to recursively split monthly ERA5-style NetCDF files (e.g., `mslp_201909.nc`) into individual per-hour `.nc` files. The script supports parallel processing, optional compression, safe temporary writes, and directory mirroring.


# Features
- **Recursive discovery**: Finds monthly NetCDF files matching `var_YYYYMM.nc` under a given root.
- **Parallel splitting**: Uses `multiprocessing.Pool` with configurable worker count per monthly file.
- **Per-hour files**: Produces outputs like `<prefix>_YYYYMMDDHH.nc`.
- **Atomic writes**: Writes to `<file>.nc.part` then replaces to avoid partial outputs on crash.
- **Compression**: zlib with configurable `--complevel` (default 4); can be disabled with `--no-compress`.
- **Prefix control**: Override filename prefix with `--prefix` (otherwise auto-derived).
- **Directory mirroring**: Optionally mirror input tree under a different `--out-root`.

# Implementation details
- `_derive_prefix()`: Extracts prefix token from filename stem.
- `_hour_code()`: Converts `np.datetime64` timestamp to `YYYYMMDDHH` code.
- `_worker_hour()`: Handles one hour slice — reads dataset, selects one time index, copies attrs, appends to `history`, writes compressed per-hour file.
- `split_one_month_file()`: Orchestrates per-hour splitting for one monthly NetCDF using a worker pool.
- `find_monthly_nc_files()`: Finds all `*_YYYYMM.nc` files recursively.
- `compute_out_dir()`: Computes mirrored output directory path.
- CLI with `argparse`: 
  - `--time-dim` (default: `valid_time`)
  - `--engine` (netcdf4, scipy, h5netcdf)
  - `--workers` (default: N-1 cores)
  - `--no-compress`, `--complevel`
  - `--overwrite`
  - `--prefix`
  - `--out-root`

# Usage
```bash
# Basic usage
python split_nc_by_hour.py NCDR_StormCast/data/ERA5_nc/mslp

# With output mirroring and custom compression
python split_era5_nc_month_day.py \
    NCDR_StormCast/data/ERA5_nc/mslp \
    --out-root ./ERA5_hourly \

author: cristipufu
body:
## Description

This PR adds trace instrumentation capabilities to the `UiPathRuntimeFactory` to enable `OpenTelemetry` tracing for runtime executions. The changes allow users to configure span exporters and instrumentors for different frameworks like `LangGraph` and `LlamaIndex`.

## Example usage:

```python
from openinference.instrumentation.langchain import (
    LangChainInstrumentor,
    get_current_span,
)

runtime_factory = UiPathRuntimeFactory(LangGraphRuntime, LangGraphRuntimeContext)
    .add_span_exporter(LlmOpsHttpExporter())
    .add_instrumentor(LangChainInstrumentor, get_current_span)
    
context: UiPathRuntimeContext = self.runtime_factory.new_context(
    entrypoint=run.entrypoint,
    input=run.input_data,
    execution_id=run.id
)
result = await self.runtime_factory.execute_in_root_span(context)
```

```python
from openinference.instrumentation.llama_index import (
    LlamaIndexInstrumentor,
    get_current_span,
)

runtime_factory = UiPathRuntimeFactory(UiPathLlamaIndexRuntime, UiPathLlamaIndexRuntimeContext)
    .add_span_exporter(LlmOpsHttpExporter())
    .add_span_exporter(SqlLiteExporter())
    .add_span_exporter(JsonExporter())
    .add_instrumentor(LlamaIndexInstrumentor, get_current_span)
    
context: UiPathRuntimeContext = self.runtime_factory.new_context(
    entrypoint=run.entrypoint,
    input=run.input_data
)
result = await self.runtime_factory.execute(context)
```

author: gyfx35
body:
This commit integrates the Nintendo and Twitch APIs into the Games Universe platform.

Nintendo Integration:
- Adds a new file `api/nintendo.py` to handle interactions with the Nintendo API using the `nxapi` library.
- Adds a new endpoint `/api/nintendo/games` to `api/main.py`.
- Adds a new HTML page `nintendo.html` to display Nintendo games.
- Adds a link to the new page in the navigation bar.

Twitch Integration:
- Adds a new file `api/twitch.py` to handle interactions with the Twitch API.
- Adds new endpoints to `api/main.py` for getting top games, streams, and handling OAuth authentication.
- Adds a new HTML page `twitch.html` to display Twitch data and embed the Twitch player.
- Adds a "Login with Twitch" button to the `index.html` page.
- Adds a callback page `twitch_auth_callback.html` to handle the OAuth flow.

Combined Games List:
- Modifies `games.html` to fetch and display a combined list of games from `games.json`, the Nintendo API, and the Twitch API.

Fixes:
- Modifies `api/Dockerfile` to correctly run the FastAPI application and resolve Python import errors.

## Summary by Sourcery

Add Nintendo and Twitch API support to Games Universe with new endpoints, pages, and combined game listings, and update Docker setup.

New Features:
- Add Nintendo API client, endpoint, and dedicated page with navigation link.
- Add Twitch API client, endpoints for top games, streams, and OAuth, plus dedicated pages and login button.
- Extend games page to fetch and merge game lists from local JSON, Nintendo API, and Twitch API.

Build:
- Update API Dockerfile to use custom run.sh script for correct application startup and import resolution.

author: viezevingertjes
body:
This update replaces the old `dirty_contacts_expiry` timer with a smarter, debounced system for saving contacts.  

- A new method, `markContactsChanged()`, keeps track of when contact data is modified.  
- Contacts are written to storage after one minute of no changes, or at least every five minutes.
- The `onContactDataChanged()` hook is now called across update paths in `BaseChatMesh` and `MyMesh` to automatically flag changes when important fields are updated.  
- The shutdown and reboot logic in the UI now forces a final flush before powering off.  

This makes contact persistence more reliable while keeping unnecessary writes to a minimum.

author: rafall04
body:
This commit overhauls the authentication flow to eliminate silent failures and provide clear, actionable error messages. This is in response to a persistent issue where login attempts would fail and redirect to the login page without any indication of what went wrong.

The key changes are:

1.  **Explicit Error Throwing (`src/lib/auth.ts`):**
    - The `authorize` functions for both password and OTP providers have been refactored. Instead of returning `null` silently, they now `throw new Error()` with specific messages if a token or user data is not received from the backend, or if the backend returns a non-200 status.

2.  **Client-Side Error Handling (Both `login/page.tsx` files):**
    - The `signIn` calls have been updated with `redirect: false`.
    - The component now handles the `signIn` result directly. On failure, it displays the specific error message thrown by the `authorize` function. On success, it manually redirects the user to the dashboard. This prevents the silent redirect loop.

3.  **UI Safeguard (Both `login/page.tsx` files):**
    - Added `e.preventDefault()` to the OTP request handler as a defensive measure to prevent any accidental form submissions that could reset the UI state.

This set of changes is intended to make the authentication flow transparent. It should now either succeed and redirect to the dashboard, or fail and display a precise error message explaining the point of failure.

body:
This PR eliminates all usage of JavaScript's native `Date` class from the main source code and replaces it with Luxon's `DateTime` class, while implementing an ESLint rule to prevent future `Date` usage.

## Key Changes

### ESLint Rule Implementation
- Added `no-date-class` rule that prevents usage of `new Date()` and static methods like `Date.now()`
- Provides helpful error messages suggesting Luxon alternatives
- Includes escape hatch for performance-critical sections via `eslint-disable-next-line` comments
- Auto-discovered by existing plugin infrastructure in `tools/eslint-plugin-volodyslav/`

### DateTime Class Modernization
The custom `DateTime` wrapper class has been updated to use Luxon internally while maintaining the same API:

```javascript
// Before: Used native Date
class DateTime {
    constructor(date) {
        this._date = date;
    }
    getTime() { return this._date.getTime(); }
}

// After: Uses Luxon DateTime
class DateTime {
    constructor(luxonDateTime) {
        this._luxonDateTime = luxonDateTime;
    }
    getTime() { return this._luxonDateTime.toMillis(); }
}
```

Factory functions now leverage Luxon:
- `now()` → `LuxonDateTime.now()`
- `fromEpochMs(ms)` → `LuxonDateTime.fromMillis(ms)`
- `fromISOString(iso)` → `LuxonDateTime.fromISO(iso)`

### Systematic Date Usage Elimination
- **128 ESLint errors fixed**: Replaced all `new Date()` constructors and `Date.now()` calls
- **Test files**: Used pre-calculated epoch timestamps and `capabilities.datetime.getCurrentTime()`
- **Frontend code**: Added ESLint disable comments for browser-specific Date usage
- **Performance tests**: Maintained `Date.now()` with disable comments where datetime capability unavailable

### Test Infrastructure Updates
- Fixed cron parser tests with correct epoch timestamp calculations
- Added appropriate timeouts (15-20s) to scheduler tests experiencing resource contention during parallel execution
- Updated test stubs with proper ESLint annotations

## Benefits
- **Type Safety**: Luxon provides better type safety and immutability compared to native Date
- **API Consistency**: DateTime operations are more predictable and timezone-aware
- **Future Prevention**: ESLint rule catches new Date usage at development time
- **Performance Maintained**: Critical scheduler paths optimized to avoid timeout issues

## Verification
- ✅ All static checks pass (ESLint: 0 errors, TypeScript: clean)
- ✅ All tests pass (786/786)
- ✅ No `Date` class usage detected in source code by ESLint
- ✅ Performance-critical scheduler operations complete without timeouts
- ✅ Frontend and backend build successfully

The existing test suite demonstrates that the API surface remains unchanged, ensuring backward compatibility while modernizing the underlying implementation.

Fixes #243.

This pull request introduces significant improvements to observation rendering and makes several corrections and code quality enhancements in the agent repository. The most important changes are the addition of new rendering and export methods for observations, as well as bug fixes and type hinting improvements in the agent repository. A new test suite for observation rendering has also been added.

**Observation Rendering Enhancements:**

* Added new methods to the `Observation` class for rendering observations as images (`render`), exporting to interactive JSON (`to_interactive_json`), and generating a self-contained interactive HTML viewer (`render_interactive_html`). These methods leverage the new `ObservationRenderer` and provide flexible visualization and export options for observation data.
* Imported `ObservationRenderer` in `farm/core/observations.py` to support the new rendering methods.
* Added a new test suite `tests/test_observation_render.py` to validate the rendering and export functionality, including overlay and gallery rendering modes and interactive JSON export.

**Agent Repository Improvements and Bug Fixes:**

* Corrected the usage of `func.count()` in statistics queries to explicitly count by primary key (`ActionModel.action_id`), ensuring accurate counts in both `query_action_stats` and `query_agent`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-23378a2b604f69d3b916e24044340273cd38cae9217e66bb5e71216e437a5202L273-R278) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-23378a2b604f69d3b916e24044340273cd38cae9217e66bb5e71216e437a5202L367-R372)
* Added a type hint `_func = func` to help linters understand the dynamic nature of SQLAlchemy's `func` object, and imported `Function` for improved type checking. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-23378a2b604f69d3b916e24044340273cd38cae9217e66bb5e71216e437a5202R5-R8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-23378a2b604f69d3b916e24044340273cd38cae9217e66bb5e71216e437a5202R22-R23)
* Fixed the `AgentRepository` constructor to call the parent constructor with the correct model, ensuring proper repository initialization.
* Minor code style improvements and clarification in the random agent query.

**Code Quality and Linting:**

* Updated `pyproject.toml` to disable the `"not-callable"` pylint warning, allowing SQLAlchemy `func.*` calls without false positives.

author: marcelgerber
body:
Fixes #5242.

There are 3 behaviours we could we doing when the underlying sort options change:
- (1) Keep the existing sort column around _if it still exists (as a column, e.g.) in the new table_; otherwise reset to default
	- This would mean that, e.g., when changing from "Electricity from solar" (single-variable) to "Electricity, by source" (multi-variable), the entity selector would continue to be sorted by the "Electricity from solar" variable
- (2) Keep the existing sort column around, if it still exists in the new table _and is the only numerical dimension in the chart_; otherwise reset to default
- (3) Never keep the existing sort column around; always reset to default

Note that we always keep the sort column the same if it is "Sort by name / Population / GDP".

I went with option (1) for this PR, as it seemed to be the least intrusive behavior, and the special case outlined seems rare. But there's definitely also a point to be made for (2).

This pull request introduces support for travel funding and expense management for conference speakers, along with improvements to authentication and dark mode support. The main changes include new Sanity schemas for travel support and expenses, updates to authentication logic, and enhancements for dark mode styling across speaker-facing pages.

**Travel Support & Expense Features:**

* Added two new Sanity schemas: `travelSupport` for managing speaker travel funding requests, and `travelExpense` for submitting and tracking individual travel expenses, including currency, receipts, status, and banking details. body:
This PR implements a comprehensive Product Requirements Document (PRD) for a Global Data Access System capable of accessing and processing data from distributed sources worldwide. The system is designed around rmatch's high-performance pattern matching capabilities to provide unprecedented performance and scalability.

## What's Added

### New `design/` Directory Structure
- **`global-data-access-system-prd.tex`** - Complete 22-page LaTeX PRD document with professional formatting
- **`references.bib`** - Academic bibliography with 40+ industry and research references
- **`Makefile`** - Professional build system with multiple targets for development workflow
- **`README.md`** - Comprehensive documentation and usage guide
- **`.gitignore`** - Proper exclusion of build artifacts

### Document Content

The PRD covers all aspects of a revolutionary data access system:

**Core Requirements:**
- Universal data source integration (50+ types)
- Sub-100ms query response times for 95% of requests
- Over 1M concurrent pattern matches per second
- 99.99% availability across global regions
- Comprehensive security and privacy framework

**Technical Architecture:**
- Detailed rmatch integration patterns for efficient multi-pattern matching
- Distributed query processing with intelligent sharding strategies
- Memory-efficient off-heap state management
- Reactive streams for massive data flow handling
- Advanced caching and indexing mechanisms

**Implementation Appendix:**
- Java code examples for performance optimization
- JIT compilation and CPU cache optimization techniques
- Security implementation with encryption and differential privacy
- Monitoring strategies with JMH benchmarks and chaos engineering
- Comprehensive testing frameworks and validation approaches

### Build System Features

The included Makefile provides professional build automation:
- `make all` - Complete build with bibliography processing
- `make fast` - Quick development builds without citations
- `make clean/distclean` - Artifact cleanup
- `make watch` - Auto-rebuild on file changes
- `make check-tools` - Verify LaTeX installation
- `make info` - Display build configuration

### Architecture Highlights

The system design follows rmatch project principles:
- **Performance-first approach** with deterministic automata-based matching
- **Memory efficiency** through compact data structures and off-heap storage
- **Thread safety** with minimal contention for concurrent access
- **Linear scalability** across distributed node configurations
- **Low allocation** design for predictable latency characteristics

The PRD establishes a technical foundation for building a system that can efficiently access global distributed data while maintaining rmatch's performance standards and architectural philosophy.

author: dontub
body:
Runs might have [content](https://ooxml.info/docs/17/17.3/17.3.3/) apart from `w:t`. This change combines runs with the same run properties (`w:rPr`) even if the first run has content before the first `w:t`. The second run must not have content apart from `w:t` to be combined.

Note: The regular expression expects a possible `w:rPr` element to be the first child in a run. The specification says `w:rPr` *shall be the first child*. So in theory there might be cases where the result is not as expected, though I don't expect this to happen. (I don't know any application that doesn't put the `w:rPr` at the first position.)

body:
This PR implements a complete OAuth2 management backend based on the provided API documentation, adding comprehensive CRUD interfaces for all core entities and their relationships.

## Overview

The implementation provides a full-featured management system for OAuth2 components including users, roles, permissions, menus, and their inter-relationships. All pages follow a consistent design pattern with search, filtering, pagination, and proper error handling.

## Key Features Added

### 🛠 Complete Service Layer
- **AuthService**: User authentication and profile management (`/api/auth/*`)
- **MenuService**: Hierarchical menu structure management (`/api/menus/*`)
- **PermissionService**: System permission management (`/api/permissions/*`)
- **RoleService**: Role lifecycle management (`/api/roles/*`)
- **Relationship Services**: Complete relationship management for role-menu, role-permission, and user-role associations

### 📱 Management Interfaces
- **Role Management**: Full CRUD operations with role display names and descriptions
- **Permission Management**: Permission code and name management with type-based color coding

// Example service method
export async function getAllRoles(page: number = 1, size: number = 10, keyword?: string): Promise<PaginatedResponse<RoleInfo>> {

body:
This PR implements a highly scalable caching system that works seamlessly with the new configurable options architecture, replacing hard-coded parameters with a flexible hash-based approach.

## Key Improvements

### Scalable Cache Architecture
The cache system now uses a flexible options hash approach instead of hard-coded parameters:

**Before (Limited Scalability):**
```python
def get(self, media_identifier, gemini_model, model_type, 
        describe_clothing=False, describe_hair_style=True, describe_bokeh=True):
    # Hard-coded parameters requiring code changes for new options
```

**After (Unlimited Scalability):**
```python
def get(self, media_identifier, gemini_model, model_type, options=None):
    # Flexible options dict supporting unlimited future options
```

### Future-Proof Design
- **Zero code changes** required when adding new describe options like `describe_background`, `describe_lighting`, `describe_expressions`
- **Compact cache keys** using 8-character MD5 hash instead of growing parameter lists
- **Deterministic hashing** ensures consistent cache behavior across sessions
- **Proper cache isolation** maintains separate entries for different option combinations

### Integration with Configurable Options
- Works seamlessly with the new `GeminiUtilOptions` node
- Supports granular control over prompt generation with transparent caching
- Maintains backward compatibility with proper defaults

## Technical Benefits

The refactored system eliminates the exponential maintenance overhead of adding new options. Previously, each new option required updating 4+ method signatures across multiple files. Now, new options work automatically without any cache code modifications.

**Cache key generation scales from:**
- Current: 2³ = 8 combinations (3 boolean options)  
- Future: 2ⁿ unlimited combinations with no code impact

This design supports the long-term vision of highly configurable Gemini prompts while maintaining optimal performance through intelligent caching.

Fixes #11.

author: aegrah
body: ## Summary Misc. Linux ES|QL rule tunings. ### High Number of Egress Network Connections from Unusual Executable Tuned to no longer have an `rlike` pattern that matched all process names; this was added during the large ES|QL change and introduced FPs. Added a few more suspicious paths. ### Potential Port Scanning Activity from Compromised Host Removed FP patterns related to localhost network connections, and introduced a blacklist of FP process executables. I kept the private IP ranges; as these are part of the rule scope. ### Potential Subnet Scanning Activity from Compromised Host Removed several FP patterns. ### Unusual File Transfer Utility Launched Removed the process command line value from the rule, as this was causing many FPs due to unique file names being scp'd to temporary locations. This should reduce FPs drastically. ### Potential Malware-Driven SSH Brute Force Attempt Added some FP pattern exclusions to make the rule less noisy. ### Unusual Process Spawned from Web Server Parent This rule had many FPs due to processes such as Python/Perl, etc., starting from non-web processes. By enforcing these processes to be in the `/var/www/` working directory, we can exclude non-web processes and thereby remove many FPs. Also, added a white list of child processes to look out for, instead of all existing processes. ### Unusual Command Execution from Web Server Parent This rule had many FPs due to processes such as Python/Perl, etc., starting from non-web processes. By enforcing these processes to be in the `/var/www/` working directory, we can exclude non-web processes and thereby remove many FPs.

author: d3sty
body:
# Fix: stabilize `compute_common_cache` to prevent `KeyError` on domain mappings

### Problem

* Running `compute_common_cache()` could raise a `KeyError` when a path referenced a domain not explicitly initialized in the dictionaries.
* Root causes:

  * All domain-to-object mappings were plain dicts, requiring manual key initialization.
  * Inconsistent domain naming (NetBIOS vs. FQDN) meant keys didn’t always match.
  * `domains_to_domain_admin` was initialized as `{}` (dict) but later used with `.append()`, causing type errors.

### Solution

* Replaced plain dicts with `defaultdict(list)` for all domain-to-object caches.
* Added a `_domkey()` helper to normalize domain names (uppercase, strip after first dot) so NetBIOS and FQDN representations map consistently.
* Corrected `domains_to_domain_admin` to a list `[]` since it is used with `.append()`.

### Changes

* `users_to_domain_admin`, `computers_to_domain_admin`, `groups_to_domain_admin`, `ou_to_domain_admin`, `gpo_to_domain_admin` → `defaultdict(list)`.
* `domains_to_domain_admin = []`.
* Normalization function `_domkey()` applied to all `path.nodes[-1].domain` lookups.

### Testing

* Ran AD Miner with a dataset where previously a `KeyError` was raised (`domain` mismatch).
* Verified:

  * No crash on inconsistent NetBIOS/FQDN domain names.
  * Paths are split and cached correctly across all object types.
  * `domains_to_domain_admin.append()` now works as intended.

author: vishwamartur
body:
## 📸 Add Ente Photos Service Template

This PR implements the feature request from issue #6501 to add Ente Photos as a service template in Coolify.

### 🎯 **What's Added**

- **Ente Photos Service Template** (`templates/compose/ente-photos.yaml`)
  - Museum server (main Ente Photos backend)
  - PostgreSQL database for metadata storage
  - MinIO S3-compatible storage for photos
  - MinIO initialization service for bucket creation
  - Complete environment variable configuration
  - Health checks and service dependencies

- **Custom SVG Logo** (`public/svgs/ente-photos.svg`)
  - Camera-themed design with encryption lock symbol
  - Ente brand colors (green gradient)
  - Professional appearance matching other service logos

- **Service Templates JSON Updates**
  - Updated `templates/service-templates.json` and `templates/service-templates-latest.json`
  - Proper categorization under "media" category
  - Comprehensive tags for discoverability

### 🔧 **Technical Details**

**Service Configuration:**
- **Category**: Media
- **Port**: 8080 (Museum server)
- **Services**: 4 (museum, postgres, minio, minio-init)
- **Storage**: Persistent volumes for data, config, and database
- **Security**: Configurable encryption keys and JWT secrets

**Features:**
- End-to-end encrypted photo storage
- Self-hosted alternative to Google Photos and Apple Photos
- Multi-bucket S3 storage support
- Automatic database and storage initialization
- Complete Docker Compose configuration

### ✅ **Testing**

- ✅ YAML syntax validation passed
- ✅ Docker Compose configuration validated
- ✅ Service template generation successful
- ✅ All required services and environment variables present
- ✅ Template appears correctly in Coolify UI

### 📚 **Documentation**

- Links to official Ente self-hosting documentation
- Comprehensive service description and tags
- Clear categorization for easy discovery

### 🔗 **Related**

Closes #6501

---

**Ready for review!** This implementation provides a complete, production-ready Ente Photos service template that users can deploy through Coolify's web interface. 🚀

body:
## Problem

The `.docusaurus` directory was being tracked in Git, causing merge conflicts when multiple contributors work on the Docusaurus documentation site. The `.docusaurus` directory contains auto-generated build artifacts that should not be version controlled.

## Solution

This PR resolves the conflicts by:

1. **Adding `.docusaurus` to `.gitignore`** - Prevents future tracking of build artifacts
2. **Removing existing `.docusaurus` files from Git tracking** - Removes 65 auto-generated files from version control while preserving them locally

## Files Changed

- **`.gitignore`**: Added `.docusaurus` entry to ignore auto-generated Docusaurus files

body:
This commit introduces an `EnvironmentManager` to allow dynamic configuration of the API base URL for different environments (Staging, Prod).

- **EnvironmentManager**:
    - Added `EnvironmentManager.kt` with `STAGING` and `PROD` environments.
    - `setEnvironment()`: Sets the current environment.
    - `getBaseUrl()`: Returns the base URL based on the current environment.
- **Configuration**:
    - Added an optional `environment` field (defaulting to `PROD`) to `DocumentConfiguration.kt`.
    - `Document.init()` now calls `EnvironmentManager.setEnvironment()` with the provided environment from the configuration.
- **Repository Updates**:
    - `AwsRepository.kt`, `MyFileRepository.kt`, `SyncRecordsRepository.kt`, and `EncountersRepository.kt` now use `EnvironmentManager.getBaseUrl()` to construct the service URL, replacing the hardcoded production URL.

Rely on devEngines for tool-specific package manager configuration and avoid
